items.title: Billy Bauer interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, March 22, 1998
items.q: I tell these stories because that’s why I try to tell them, that’s what I did with music you know. See because he said you know like what makes Sammy run, I think there was a story like that

ctx.x: Did he lose his job during that time? © Fillius Jazz Archive -9-

No, no he didn’t lose — I guess he did lose his job because that’s all he was doing. See he wound up to be — the whole family was printers outside of me. So his father wanted him to be a printer, and he became a printer. But then his father was older with his father’s brother, it was an uncle I guess of mine, but I didn’t know him very much, but they were old-time. And my grandfather couldn’t get along with his brother. And they had a fight. So that means my father and him were out. So my grandfather, he didn’t…
That’s a great story. I had something about you playing with a fellow named Jerry Wald?
